items.title: Fake Ads on Social Media Are Trapping Shoppers — FTC Warns
items.summary: The Federal Trade Commission warns that ads on social media platforms are not checked for scams. Crooks run fake ads on Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok using stolen product photos and made-up reviews — you pay but the item never arrives, or it shows up broken. The FTC says this happens every day and costs people real money (FTC.gov, August 2026). Before buying from any social media ad, search the company name plus "scam" on Google. If the company has no real website or phone number, don't buy. Always use a credit card so you can dispute the charge.

items.title: Turn any lamp into a smart lamp for 10 dollars — TP-Link Kasa Smart Plug lets you control it from your phone with the free Kasa app
items.summary: Buy a TP-Link Kasa Smart Plug EP25 for about 10 dollars at Amazon or Walmart, plug it into any wall outlet, plug in your lamp, and control it from the free Kasa Smart app on your phone — set schedules, turn lights on from bed, or flip them off from the grocery store.
items.truth: I see people spend 200 dollars on smart home systems when all they really want is to turn the porch light on before they get home. A 10-dollar smart plug does that. You do not need a hub, you do not need a subscription, and you do not need to call me. Download the free Kasa Smart app from the Play Store or App Store, follow the 2-minute setup, and you are done.

items.title: Can't read the small text on your computer screen? Windows Magnifier makes everything bigger free — press the Windows key and Plus to zoom in instantly
items.summary: Press the Windows key and the Plus sign (+) to zoom in on anything on your screen, press Windows key and Minus to zoom back out, and press Windows key and Escape to turn Magnifier off — built into every Windows 10 and 11 computer, no download needed.
items.truth: I cannot tell you how many customers come in thinking they need a new monitor because the text is too small. They do not — they just need Magnifier. It has been built into Windows for years and almost nobody knows it exists. Press Windows key + Plus and your entire screen zooms in. You can even choose a lens mode that works like a magnifying glass that follows your mouse around the screen.

items.title: Fake Postcards Promise VA Benefits — It's a Scam Stealing Veterans' Personal Info
items.summary: Scammers are mailing official-looking postcards to veterans across the country, promising free monthly VA benefit payments. The postcard includes a phone number and website asking for your Social Security number or bank details to "verify eligibility." The real VA never contacts veterans this way — they already have your information on file. If you or a loved one receives one of these postcards, do not call the number or visit the website. Instead, verify any VA communication through va.gov or call 1-800-827-1000 directly. Report the scam to ReportFraud.ftc.gov. — Source: FTC, August 24, 2026

items.title: Windows 11 August update causes games to crash and PCs to reboot — Microsoft is working on a patch
items.summary: If your PC crashes, freezes, or reboots by itself after the August Windows update, you're not alone — Microsoft has confirmed the issue and a proper fix is on the way. Don't uninstall the update, which leaves you vulnerable to 400+ security holes; just wait for Microsoft's patch within the next few weeks.

items.title: Chrome 153 ships with a critical security patch — take 30 seconds to update now
items.summary: Open Chrome, click the three dots at top right, click Help, then About Google Chrome — the update installs automatically when you open that page.

items.title: Brushing Scams: Why Random Packages Are Showing Up at Your Door
items.summary: A package shows up on your porch you never ordered. The FTC warned on August 20 that this is a "brushing" scam — sellers send you free junk using your name so they can post a fake five-star review in your name. Some packages include QR codes that lead to fake websites designed to steal your information. If you receive a package you did not order, do not scan any codes inside. Check your online accounts for unfamiliar orders and report it free at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

items.title: CISA Flags 4 Actively Exploited Flaws — Update Your Mac and Windows Now
items.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added four new actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on August 18. Two affect Apple Macs and two affect Windows. Update macOS at System Settings > General > Software Update and Windows at Settings > Windows Update tonight.

items.title: Fake Bill-Payment Websites Are Tricking You Through Search Ads
items.summary: The FTC just warned that scammers are buying fake ads at the top of Google and Bing that look like your electric company, insurance provider, or bank. You search for "pay my light bill," click the first result, enter your account number and card, and the money goes to a crook instead of your real company. Always scroll past the ads and look for the official web address you already know — or call the number on your paper bill. Report fraud at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. (Source: FTC.gov, August 17, 2026)

items.title: Stop Windows from begging you to buy Microsoft 365 — turn off the subscription nag screens
items.summary: Press the Windows key, type **Notifications** and press Enter. Scroll down and turn off notifications from **Microsoft 365 (Office)** and **Get Help**. That kills the pop-ups permanently — takes 30 seconds.

items.title: Turn your old scanner into a clean PDF maker — NAPS2 is free and has no watermarks
items.summary: Download **NAPS2** (Not Another PDF Scanner 2) free at **naps2.org**. Plug in your scanner, open NAPS2, click the green **Scan** button, and save your document as a PDF or image file. No account, no watermarks, no ads, no subscription.
